title: TS-04 Black-box acceptance runner and demo CLI
description:
## Slice 2 ticket 4 of 40, phase notes: paths use `conversation/` (the workspace as it is on develop). Design source: `git show origin/docs/typescript-control-plane:docs/TYPESCRIPT_CONTROL_PLANE.md` (section 8, row 4); read sections 0.3, 2, 3 and 6 as needed. Read AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING_AGENT.md first. Never read or write `project/`; use `kbs` only.

## Goal
Port the Python integration-test runner and the demo CLI to TypeScript scripts that speak only HTTP to a deployed environment (so the spec never goes dark during the migration): sign in, create bot, create channel, post, read the SSE stream, reload.

## Kind
mechanical-port: the Python source below is the specification. Keep its structure, names (camelCase), branches and messages. Do not redesign anything.

## Branch and commit
```text
git fetch origin
git switch -c ts/04-black-box-acceptance-runner-and-demo-cli origin/develop
...work, then...
git add <only the files listed under Files>
git commit -m "feat(conversation): black-box acceptance runner and demo CLI

Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"
git push -u origin ts/04-black-box-acceptance-runner-and-demo-cli
```
Do NOT open a pull request; the orchestrator opens it. Commit messages contain no emojis.

## Files to create or change
- `conversation/bin/acceptance.ts`
- `conversation/bin/chat.ts`
- `conversation/src/acceptance/sigv4.ts`
- `conversation/src/acceptance/sse-parser.ts`
- `conversation/src/acceptance/http-client.ts`
- `conversation/features-support/steps/demo-cli.steps.ts`
- `conversation/test/sse-parser.test.ts`

## Exported interface and error behavior
`parseSseFrames(chunk: string, carry: string): {frames: SseFrame[]; carry: string}` with `SseFrame = {event: string; id: string | null; data: string}`; comment lines starting `:` are ignored. `signSigV4(request: {method; url; headers; body}, credentials, region, service): Record<string,string>`. `bin/acceptance.ts --environment development|staging|production` exits 1 on first failed check and prints which. The environment base URL is read from the env var named in AGENTS.local.md (`CHATTICUS_<ENV>_BASE_URL`); if unset it exits 2 with the message `base url for <env> not set`.

General rules: TypeScript ESM, `.ts` import suffixes as in conversation/src/storage/; tabs for indentation as in existing files; long clear names; no line comments; TSDoc on exported symbols; no emojis. Each Python exception class used by a ported function becomes an exported `Error` subclass with the same name and the same message text. Failures are thrown, never returned as magic values, unless the Python returned them.

## Python source to port (keep structure; read it fully before writing)
- `python/src/chatticus/integration_test/runner.py (whole file)`
- `python/src/chatticus/integration_test/sigv4.py (55 lines, SigV4 session exchange)`
- `python/src/chatticus/integration_test/sse.py (SSE frame parser)`
- `python/src/chatticus/thin_turn_conversation.py (whole file, the demo conversation flow)`
- `python/src/chatticus/integration_test/lambda_handler.py (read for the CLI arguments only)`
Rule: mechanical ports keep the Python file's structure and cite the Python line range in the commit body. Behavior that no scenario encodes is still kept.

## Behavior spec (Gherkin, ported unchanged)
Existing features that must pass under cucumber-js when this ticket closes. Do NOT edit these `.feature` files except where this ticket says a behavior changed.

### features/demo_cli.feature  (all 4 scenarios)
Scenarios: Post a message and watch tokens through completion; Reconnect after a dropped stream replays stored chunks; A second turn commits the streamed answer after a prior bot greeting; List in-flight turns after a Front Door recycle
Step texts to implement in TypeScript (exact step text, then the Python step that implements it today):
```text
an empty control plane   <-  features/steps/control_plane_steps.py:48
tenant "anthus" user "ryan" has a channel with a named bot "Assistant"   <-  features/steps/messaging_steps.py:343
user "ryan" of tenant "anthus" posts "hello" addressed to bot "Assistant" on the channel   <-  features/steps/messaging_steps.py:368
the demo client watches the turn stream for that channel   <-  features/steps/demo_cli_steps.py:54
the demo client saw turn tokens in order   <-  features/steps/demo_cli_steps.py:87
the demo client saw the committed bot reply   <-  features/steps/demo_cli_steps.py:99
the demo client watches the turn stream until one token arrives then drops   <-  features/steps/demo_cli_steps.py:63
the demo client reconnects to the same turn from stored chunks   <-  features/steps/demo_cli_steps.py:75
the demo client saw turn tokens in order without duplicate sequences   <-  features/steps/demo_cli_steps.py:140
bot "Assistant" completes one turn   <-  features/steps/messaging_steps.py:831
user "ryan" of tenant "anthus" posts "what is two plus two" addressed to bot "Assistant" on the channel   <-  features/steps/messaging_steps.py:368
the committed bot reply matches the streamed tokens   <-  features/steps/demo_cli_steps.py:111
the committed bot reply is not the prior bot greeting on the channel   <-  features/steps/demo_cli_steps.py:123
an empty control plane backed by a durable messaging store with HTTP   <-  features/steps/control_plane_steps.py:523
tenant "anthus" user "ryan" has a bot named "Assistant"   <-  features/steps/control_plane_steps.py:280
tenant "anthus" user "ryan" opens a channel with bots:   <-  features/steps/messaging_steps.py:285
user "ryan" of tenant "anthus" posts a fence probe addressed to bot "Assistant" without enqueueing a turn job   <-  features/steps/messaging_steps.py:430
a recycled Front Door serves the same messaging store   <-  features/steps/control_plane_steps.py:538
the demo client lists in-flight turns for user "ryan" of tenant "anthus":   <-  features/steps/demo_cli_steps.py:153
```
Cucumber expressions: convert each Python `{name}` parse pattern to `{string}`, `{int}` or `{word}` using `npx tsx conversation/bin/convert-step-pattern.ts '<pattern>'` (from ticket 3) and review the output by hand. Step text must not change unless behavior changed. Steps call `this.api` (HTTP via `app.request()`) for HTTP steps and the same domain functions the routes call for direct steps; steps never reach into a store.
Step file(s) to write: under `conversation/features-support/steps/` as named in Files above (at most about 400 lines each; split by subject).

Failing run first (required):
```text
1. Write or port the step file(s) and any new .feature file.
2. cd conversation && npx cucumber-js ../features/<feature>.feature   -> confirm the scenarios FAIL for the right reason (missing production code, not a typo in a step). Save the first failing summary line for the commit body.
3. Write the smallest production code that passes. Re-run until green.
```
Manifest: when EVERY scenario of a feature is covered by this ticket (not marked partial above), add `features/<name>.feature` to `features/ported-features.txt` and add `<name>` to the alternation in `python/behave.ini` `exclude_re` (the manifest vitest `conversation/test/ported-features-manifest.test.ts` fails if they disagree). For a partial feature leave the manifest alone; the ticket named in the note finishes it. To run a partial feature, pass the path and `--name '<scenario>'` to cucumber-js; if CLI paths do not override the config paths, stop and report.

## Dependencies (blocked-by)
- ticket 1 (chatticus-9a2e3f): Workspace CI gates: dry-run gate and manifest checks (rename deferred); provides what its Files section lists.

## Verify
```text
cd conversation && npm run typecheck && npm test && npx cucumber-js ../features/<each feature of this ticket>.feature
```
moto setup (copied from the `conversation` job in .github/workflows/ci.yml):
```text
python -m pip install "moto[server]==5.2.3"
nohup moto_server -p 5555 > moto.log 2>&1 &
for i in $(seq 1 30); do if (echo > /dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/5555) 2>/dev/null; then break; fi; sleep 1; done
export CHATTICUS_TEST_AWS_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:5555
```
Install once at the repo root: `npm ci`. Stop moto when done: `pkill -f "moto_server -p 5555"`.
If the ticket added a feature to the manifest also run `cd conversation && npx cucumber-js` (full manifest) and `cd python && behave` is NOT required for ported features, but run `cd python && black --check src ../features tests && ruff check src ../features tests` if you touched anything under python/ or features/steps/.
Final cleanup before pushing:
```text
git status
```
Make sure NO `.orig`, `.rej`, `node_modules`, `build/`, `dist/`, `moto.log`, `.venv` or other stray files are staged: `git diff --cached --name-only | grep -E '\.orig$|\.rej$|node_modules|(^|/)build/|(^|/)dist/|moto\.log|\.venv'` must print nothing.

## Notes
Never run these against staging or production in this ticket; only unit-test the parser and run the demo_cli feature, which uses a fake HTTP server defined in the Python step file (read it and port it as a node:http server in the step file).

## Stop rules
If anything in this ticket is wrong, ambiguous, impossible, or contradicted by the code you find (a Python line range does not match, a step has no Python match, a library API differs from what is written, a scenario cannot pass without changing its text), STOP and report to the orchestrator with the exact file, line and observation. Never improvise, never weaken or delete a scenario to make it pass, never add a fallback or a compatibility branch.

## Python to delete
No production Python is deleted by this ticket (the one big deletion is ticket 40). The only deletions allowed: the per-feature step file of each feature newly added to the manifest, because the manifest vitest requires it: features/steps/demo_cli_steps.py (if it exists). Shared step files (control_plane_steps.py, capability_policy_steps.py, messaging_steps.py, organization_steps.py and the like) are never edited here; the last ticket that uses them leaves them for ticket 40.
right_now_summary: The TypeScript acceptance runner and demo CLI still need to be ported and tested.
